blocks.text: Practice short questions for the whole of Unit 7 (Kinematics of Motion in a Straight Line (TOC: 'Kinematics')), arranged by the unit's sections, in the style of a 2-mark Board short question. Each one is solved briefly, step by step.

blocks.prompt: 1 Define kinematics. Which tools of calculus does it use?
blocks.explanation: Kinematics is the branch of mechanics that describes the motion of objects without considering the causes of motion. It uses differentiation (to get velocity and acceleration as rates of change) and integration (to go back from acceleration to velocity and from velocity to displacement).

book_ref.quote: Kinematics is the branch of mechanics that describes the motion of objects without considering the causes of motion.

blocks.prompt: 2 Define rectilinear motion and give two examples.
blocks.explanation: The motion of a particle along a straight line is called rectilinear motion. Examples: a car on a straight road; a lift going up and down; a stone dropped from a roof.

book_ref.quote: The motion of a particle along a straight line is called rectilinear motion.

blocks.prompt: 3 Define a scalar quantity. Give two scalar quantities used in kinematics.
blocks.explanation: Scalar quantities are completely described by magnitude only (number with unit); they have no direction. Examples: distance (total length of the path travelled) and speed (distance covered per unit time).

book_ref.quote: Scalar quantities are those that are completely described by magnitude only

blocks.prompt: 4 Convert (i) \(90\) km/h into m/s (ii) \(12\) m/s into km/h.

book_ref.quote: Speed: Rate at which distance is covered per unit time, irrespective of direction.

blocks.prompt: 5 Define a vector quantity and name three vector quantities of kinematics.
blocks.explanation: Vector quantities are described by both magnitude and direction. In kinematics: displacement, velocity and acceleration.

book_ref.quote: Vector quantities are described by both magnitude and direction.

blocks.prompt: 6 Distinguish between distance and displacement.
blocks.explanation: Distance is a scalar (path length); displacement is a vector (change in position).

book_ref.quote: Change in position, from the initial to the final position

rows: Total length of the path travelled
Change in position, from the initial to the final position
Depends only on the initial and final positions
Can be positive, negative or zero

blocks.prompt: 7 Distinguish between speed and velocity.
blocks.explanation: Speed is a scalar; velocity is a vector whose magnitude is the speed.

book_ref.quote: Its sign shows the direction of motion

rows: Its sign shows the direction of motion
Velocity = speed in a given direction

blocks.prompt: 8 A man walks \(8\) km north and then \(5\) km south along a straight road. Find the distance travelled and his displacement.
blocks.explanation: Distance \(= 8 + 5 = 13\) km. Taking north positive, displacement \(= 8 + (-5) = 3\) km, i.e. \(3\) km north.

book_ref.quote: Displacement is change in position of a particle represented by a vector from initial to final position.

blocks.prompt: 9 Define average velocity and average speed.
blocks.explanation: Average velocity \(= \dfrac{\text{total displacement}}{\text{total time}} = \dfrac{\Delta x}{\Delta t}\). Average speed \(= \dfrac{\text{total distance travelled}}{\text{total time}}\).

book_ref.quote: defined as the total displacement divided by the total time taken

blocks.prompt: 10 A runner runs \(400\) m east in \(50\) s and then \(100\) m west in \(25\) s. Find his average speed and average velocity.
blocks.explanation: Total distance and total time first, then displacement with signs.

book_ref.quote: The average speed of an object is defined as the total distance travelled divided by the total time taken:

steps: Total distance \(= 400 + 100 = 500\) m; total time \(= 50 + 25 = 75\) s
East positive: displacement \(= 400 - 100 = 300\) m; average velocity \(= \frac{300}{75} = 4\) m/s
blocks.final_answer: Average speed \(\frac{20}{3} \approx 6.67\) m/s; average velocity \(4\) m/s towards the east.

blocks.prompt: 11 Define instantaneous velocity and instantaneous speed.
blocks.explanation: Instantaneous velocity is the rate of change of displacement with respect to time at a given instant: \(v(t) = \frac{dx}{dt}\). Instantaneous speed is its magnitude: \(|v(t)| = \left|\frac{dx}{dt}\right|\).

book_ref.quote: is the rate of change of displacement with respect to time at a given instant

blocks.prompt: 12 The position of a particle is \(x(t) = t^{3} - 3t^{2} + 2\) (m, s). Find its velocity and acceleration at \(t = 3\) s.

book_ref.quote: Rate of change of velocity with respect to time is called acceleration.

blocks.prompt: 13 If \(x(t) = 5t - t^{2}\) (m, s), find the velocity and the speed at \(t = 4\) s.
blocks.explanation: \(v = 5 - 2t\), \(v(4) = -3\) m/s (moving in the negative direction); speed \(= |-3| = 3\) m/s.

book_ref.quote: Instantaneous speed is the magnitude of instantaneous velocity

blocks.prompt: 14 A particle moves so that \(x(t) = 2t^{3} - 15t^{2} + 36t\) (m, s). When is it momentarily at rest?

book_ref.quote: momentarily at rest (this is where a particle can turn back)

blocks.explanation: Use the chain rule through \(x\).

blocks.prompt: 17 The position of a particle is \(x(t) = 3\cos t\). Find its velocity and acceleration at \(t = \frac{\pi}{2}\).
blocks.explanation: \(v = \frac{dx}{dt} = -3\sin t\), \(v\left(\frac{\pi}{2}\right) = -3\). \(a = \frac{dv}{dt} = -3\cos t\), \(a\left(\frac{\pi}{2}\right) = 0\).

blocks.prompt: 18 What does the slope of a displacement-time graph represent? What do a rising, a horizontal and a falling straight line show?
blocks.explanation: Slope \(= \frac{dx}{dt} =\) velocity. Rising straight line: constant \(v > 0\) (moving forward); horizontal line: \(v = 0\) (at rest); falling straight line: constant \(v < 0\) (moving in the opposite direction).

book_ref.quote: represents velocity of the particle.

blocks.prompt: 19 A displacement-time graph is a straight line from \((0, 10)\) to \((5, 35)\) (\(t\) in s, \(x\) in m). Find the velocity.
blocks.explanation: Velocity \(=\) slope \(= \frac{35 - 10}{5 - 0} = \frac{25}{5} = 5\) m/s (uniform, since the graph is straight).

blocks.explanation: Slope of each segment in km/min, then multiply by 60.

blocks.final_answer: OA \(4\) km/h, AB \(0\) km/h, BC \(-6\) km/h (walking back).

blocks.prompt: 21 For the same walker (\(O(0, 0)\), \(A(30, 2)\), \(B(40, 2)\), \(C(60, 0)\); minutes, km), find the average speed and the average velocity for the whole journey.
blocks.explanation: Distance \(= 2 + 2 = 4\) km in \(60\) min \(= 1\) h (rest included): average speed \(= 4\) km/h. He ends at the start, so displacement \(= 0\) and average velocity \(= 0\).

book_ref.quote: Waiting time counts in the total time of a journey.

blocks.prompt: 22 A van drives for \(1.5\) h at an average velocity of \(60\) km/h, stops for \(0.5\) h, and then drives a further \(30\) km in the same direction in \(1\) h. Find its total displacement and its average velocity.
blocks.explanation: First drive \(= 60 \times 1.5 = 90\) km; total displacement \(= 90 + 30 = 120\) km; total time \(= 1.5 + 0.5 + 1 = 3\) h; average velocity \(= \frac{120}{3} = 40\) km/h.

blocks.prompt: 23 What do the slope and the area under a velocity-time graph represent?
blocks.explanation: Slope \(= \frac{dv}{dt} =\) acceleration. Area under the graph from \(t_{1}\) to \(t_{2}\) \(= \int_{t_{1}}^{t_{2}} v\,dt =\) displacement in that interval.

book_ref.quote: Acceleration = Slope of velocity time graph

blocks.prompt: 24 Show that the area under a velocity-time graph from \(t = t_{1}\) to \(t = t_{2}\) is the displacement in that interval.
blocks.explanation: Write the area as an integral and use \(v = \frac{dx}{dt}\).

book_ref.quote: then from integral calculus:

blocks.final_answer: Hence proved: the area \(A = x(t_{2}) - x(t_{1})\) is the displacement from \(t_{1}\) to \(t_{2}\).

blocks.prompt: 25 A particle starts from rest and reaches \(12\) m/s uniformly in \(3\) s, keeps this velocity up to \(t = 10\) s and then comes to rest uniformly at \(t = 12\) s. Find its acceleration in the first \(3\) s and the total displacement.
blocks.explanation: Acceleration \(=\) slope \(= \frac{12}{3} = 4\) m/s\(^{2}\). Displacement \(=\) area of trapezium \(= \frac{1}{2}(12 + 7) \times 12 = 114\) m (parallel sides \(12\) s and \(10 - 3 = 7\) s, height \(12\)).

book_ref.quote: If \(a = \frac{dv}{dt} = \text{constant} > 0\)

blocks.explanation: Find where the graph crosses the time axis, then the two triangle areas.

steps: Displacement \(= A_{1} - A_{2} = 7.5\) m; distance \(= A_{1} + A_{2} = 19.5\) m

blocks.prompt: 37 What is free fall? Which equations of motion are used for upward and for downward motion?
blocks.explanation: Motion under gravity alone, with air resistance neglected, along a vertical line. Downward: \(a = g\) (\(v = u + gt\), \(x = ut + \frac{1}{2}gt^{2}\)); upward: \(a = -g\) (\(v = u - gt\), \(x = ut - \frac{1}{2}gt^{2}\)), with \(g = 9.8\) m/s\(^{2}\).

book_ref.quote: the motion is called free fall or free vertical motion

blocks.prompt: 38 A stone is dropped from a height of \(122.5\) m. Find the time to reach the ground and the velocity on impact.

book_ref.quote: (Free Fall from Rest) A stone is dropped from the top of a tower

blocks.prompt: 39 A ball is thrown vertically upward with \(24.5\) m/s. Find the time to reach the top and the maximum height.

book_ref.quote: Time to the top \(= \frac{u}{g}\); maximum height \(= \frac{u^{2}}{2g}\).

blocks.prompt: 40 A particle is projected vertically upward with velocity \(u\). Show that the time to reach the highest point is \(\frac{u}{g}\) and the maximum height is \(\frac{u^{2}}{2g}\).
blocks.explanation: At the top \(v = 0\); use the upward equations with \(a = -g\).

book_ref.quote: If a particle is projected upward, its velocity decreases uniformly due to gravity

steps: At the top \(v = 0\): \(0 = u - gt \Rightarrow t = \dfrac{u}{g}\)
blocks.final_answer: Hence proved: time to the top \(\frac{u}{g}\), maximum height \(\frac{u^{2}}{2g}\).
